deep.reconstruction: This page contains no mathematics by Riemann. The image shows page 4 of a printed Italian newspaper. The previous page's text (Palazzo Madama, the Accademia Albertina, the Royal Palace staircase, via Nizza) points to Turin. The page carries four items. (1) The end of a report on an ascent by Nadar's balloon 'Le Géant': four passengers, two of them from Lyon; the balloon heads south-west and lands at Saint-Agrève. (2) 'Un toro furioso', taken from the Avenir National: a 66-year-old herdsman is killed by a bull on 25 June. (3) 'Portafoglio', a comic anecdote: a railway worker comes home early, leaves in the dark wearing the trousers of his wife's lover (the lawyer Z.), and finds a full purse in them. (4) The start of 'Scala del palazzo reale', on the restoration of the Turin royal palace staircase with paintings by Ferri, Gastaldi and Bertini. The remark on the previous page that the Senate has been 'removed' from Palazzo Madama suggests a date after the capital moved to Florence (1865). That fits Riemann's stays in Italy (1862–66). The sheet was evidently reused as scrap or wrapping paper in the 'R.AbelTheta' bundle. The real manuscript content is presumably on the other side of the sheet or on neighbouring folios. The next page holds the theta-characteristic product identities (ϑ abce_3 … etc.). Those identities belong to Riemann's study of theta functions with half-period characteristics in genus 3 and 4 (cf. his work on Abelian functions and theta relations), but they are not on this page. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically. The page is relevant only as physical and contextual evidence: Italian newsprint, plausibly from the mid-1860s, used during Riemann's Italian period.
